訪.meaning: Your grandma arrives by boat, unfurls her <part>sail</part> in your front garden and gives a long <part>speech</part> from the deck about how much you've grown. She stays for tea, three naps and two weeks. That's how she likes to <kanji>call on</kanji> you.
訪.on: You hint it's time to go by spraying her deck with the garden <sound>ho</sound>se.
訪.kun: Next year she's back, with an <sound>o</sound>ctopus on <sound>to</sound>p of the mast and a basket of yu<sound>zu</sound> fruit for you.

脳.meaning: A <part>villain</part> wears a bucket on his head to stop his ideas leaking out. It fails: one night <part>fireworks</part> burst out of the bucket and spell his whole evil plan across the <part>moon</part>. Now the entire town can read his <kanji>brain</kanji>.
脳.on: A garden <sound>gno</sound>me reads the plan in the sky and calls the police.
脳.kun: '<sound>No</sound>!' he groans, hurling a yu<sound>zu</sound> at a <sound>roo</sound>k that is cawing his plan to the whole town.

聴.meaning: A shy whale sings at the bottom of the sea, so a fisherman lowers a <part>net</part> with <part>ten</part> seashells tied to it, presses one <part>ear</part> to the rope and holds his breath. The song trembles up the line and straight into his <part>heart</part>. For once he stops talking, to <kanji>listen</kanji>.
聴.on: The tune is so lovely that his collar feels as tight as a <sound>cho</sound>ker.
聴.kun: Back on shore, he hums it to a <sound>ki</sound>wi bird and the ship's <sound>coo</sound>k, who lean in close.

講.meaning: A professor refuses to use the stage, so she climbs the wobbly <part>scaffolding</part> outside the hall and gives her <part>speech</part> through a third-floor window, swaying with every point. Students below take notes with their necks craned. It's the scariest <kanji>lecture</kanji> on campus.
講.on: She points at her slides with an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne, dripping on the front row.

京.meaning: The king builds his city on a giant cooking pot: the palace sits on the <part>lid</part>, the market squeezes into the pot's <part>mouth</part>, and a <part>little</part> village dangles from the legs below. Every road leads up to the lid, where the king sits waving. It's the nation's <kanji>capital</kanji>.
京.on: From the lid, the king bangs a gong and calls out his city's name, <sound>Kyo</sound>to, holding its first part so long it echoes down the pot to the village.
京.kun: Down there, a <sound>mee</sound>rkat knits <sound>ya</sound>rn into a scarf for a shivering <sound>ko</sound>ala.

版.meaning: Before each print run, the old editor holds a <part>tai chi pose</part> on the roof. Today a rival paper prints the <part>anti</part> of every headline he wrote, so he flows slowly downstairs and prints a reply, then a reply to their reply. By sunset six versions are on sale, each a fresh <kanji>edition</kanji>.
版.on: The ink smells sweet, because the cheap print shop has mixed it with <sound>hon</sound>ey.

暮.meaning: The <part>sunset</part> is so lovely that a second <part>sun</part> sinks down to join it and refuses to leave, peeking over the hill. Owls wake up confused, bats don't know whether to go out, and the sky stays purple for hours. The whole town is stuck in <kanji>twilight</kanji>.
暮.on: An old man waters his <sound>bo</sound>nsai on the porch, glad of the long purple glow.
暮.kun: Finally a <sound>coo</sound>k gives up waiting and lights the lamps as the day grows dark.
